gloss: to start moving; to get going

definitions.gloss: to start moving; to begin to move; to get into motion
definitions.explanation: To begin moving after being still. Used for physical objects, vehicles, and figuratively for projects, plans, or situations that begin to progress.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}がゆっくり{動|うご}き{出|だ}した。
{計画|けいかく}がやっと{動|うご}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The plan finally got into motion.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると、{冬眠|とうみん}していた{動物|どうぶつ}たちが{動|うご}き{出|だ}す。
examples.english: When spring comes, the hibernating animals begin to stir.

notes:
FORMATION:
Compound verb: {動|うご}く (to move) + {出|だ}す (to begin). The ～{出|だ}す pattern indicates the beginning of an action: {歩|ある}き{出|だ}す (to start walking), {泣|な}き{出|だ}す (to start crying), {降|ふ}り{出|だ}す (to start raining).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ゆっくり{動|うご}き{出|だ}す (to start moving slowly)
- いよいよ{動|うご}き{出|だ}す (to finally get going)
- {一斉|いっせい}に{動|うご}き{出|だ}す (to all start moving at once)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {動|うご}き{始|はじ}める: to begin to move — synonymous, slightly more formal
- {始動|しどう}する: to start up — technical, for machines and engines
- {発進|はっしん}する: to depart, to set off — for vehicles
